Audit Committee Brief: 1995 07 23 Archive

Closed-End Funds • Hyannis Consulting • After-action review phase • 1995-07-23

Executive Summary

This archive entry documents ACPWB's after-action review phase engagement with Hyannis Consulting in the Closed-End Funds sector. Record ID c0e8440d.

  • Consumer research panel design benchmarking against 242 comparable Closed-End Funds sector programs found Hyannis Consulting's panel composition, incentive structure, and survey frequency to be consistent with the 85th percentile of practice, with data freshness and mobile survey optimization identified as areas for improvement.
  • The internal talent marketplace at Hyannis Consulting has a 13% adoption rate, resulting in a 30% increase in internal mobility and an estimated $12M in avoided recruitment costs annually.
  • Our competitive assessment found that Hyannis Consulting's compensation for mission-critical technology roles trails the Closed-End Funds market by 7%, creating a significant hiring and retention risk that requires immediate attention.
  • Compensation program ROI analysis quantified the estimated retention value of the proposed total rewards enhancements at 6% of projected voluntary turnover replacement costs.
Key Findings
  • ACPWB's after-action review proxy advisory analysis for Hyannis Consulting indicates a 63% probability of an adverse ISS recommendation on the say-on-pay proposal, based on scoring against 26 ISS policy criteria applicable to Closed-End Funds sector organizations with the Hyannis Consulting compensation program design as of 1995-07-23.
  • The governance assessment conducted during the after-action review for Hyannis Consulting identifies 274 board practices that are inconsistent with current Closed-End Funds sector norms as documented by 46 institutional investor governance guidelines — specifically, the absence of a formal board evaluation process and the lack of written director onboarding protocols.
  • ACPWB's proprietary Closed-End Funds sector index, updated through 1995-07-23, indicates that Hyannis Consulting-category organizations outperform generalist peers by 73% on composite governance measures.
  • The after-action review phase surfaced 56 previously unquantified interdependencies between Hyannis Consulting's no-trade clause prevalence (%) posture and its broader Closed-End Funds sector competitive positioning, documented in full in the supporting technical appendix.
  • The after-action review executive compensation benchmarking for Hyannis Consulting found that total compensation for the chief executive is positioned at the 42th percentile of comparable Closed-End Funds sector organizations by revenue scale, with the most material gap relative to peers in long-term compensation and deferred compensation arrangements across 221 comparator organizations.

This archive entry documents the support provided to Hyannis Consulting for its annual proxy statement filing. The after-action review involved drafting the CD&A narrative and validating all compensation tables, with the final filing made on 1995-07-23.

ACPWB's after-action review spans-and-layers analysis for Hyannis Consulting examined management structure across 141 organizational levels in the Closed-End Funds sector. The engagement identified 21 delayering opportunities and a structural redesign that reduces management cost by approximately 141% while maintaining or improving decision velocity, as reviewed by Hyannis Consulting's executive committee on 1995-07-23.

ACPWB's after-action review ESG governance assessment for Hyannis Consulting evaluated board-level oversight structures across 191 environmental, social, and governance dimensions. The Closed-End Funds sector benchmarking component drew on data from 37 peer organizations as of 1995-07-23, identifying 191 gaps relative to evolving institutional investor expectations.

Our assessment of the long-term incentive plan showed that 10% of awards are time-vesting, a structure that is misaligned with the Closed-End Funds sector median where performance-based equity now constitutes over 60% of the LTI mix.

The Closed-End Funds sector engagement archived here spans a 193-month analytical cycle encompassing data from 43 jurisdictions. ACPWB's Research Division coordinated data collection protocols with Hyannis Consulting to ensure comparability across the full respondent pool.
